FinAstro 2027 - calendar

5,209 rows over 11 instruments · 1,854 carrying a verdict, 3,355 with none · confidence untested on every row
Read this first. Financial astrology is a speculative interpretive framework. The dates and conditions in this calendar are computed from an ephemeris and ported from a 2026 source document; the interpretations are that source's claims, carried verbatim or absent. Nothing here is a forecast, a prediction, or investment advice, and no confidence has been raised above `untested` for any row.
What this calendar is, and what it is not — the epistemic apparatus

Two layers, never merged. The astronomy layer is computed from an ephemeris: positions, ingresses, stations, rises, eclipses. The interpretation layer is the 2026 source's own claims, carried verbatim or absent. Nothing in this file infers a market outcome from a planetary position.

Certainty grades

Every astronomy record carries one. A is computed exact under a minute; B is computed but definition-sensitive; C depends on something unevidenced — and C has two grounds, which have different remedies and are named on every record and every rule:

  • undocumented_source_rule — the rule itself is not recoverable from the source
  • parameter_not_constrained_by_evidence — the method is sound; a fitted parameter has fewer constraints than free parameters

A station is frame-free: it is where the longitude is stationary, and no parameter stands between the sky and the instant. A crossing of 0.6583 deg/day is only as meaningful as 0.6583 is.

Claim tags

Each rule's verdict carries the tag its own words earn: Classical where the source states it plainly, Observed where the source hedges its own claim, Framework where it is a modern practitioner extension. A rule that prints no inference carries no tag, because an unstated claim has nothing to tag.

Tiers, and the five values they take

  • book_derived — 47 rows
  • cross_market_localized — 648 rows
  • no_rule — 3,285 rows
  • source_backed — 1,019 rows
  • venue_shifted — 210 rows

cross_market_localized is a rule the source authored for Indian equities, applied to a different market (SPX, NDX). venue_shifted is the SAME instrument, same rule, same sky, differing only in which venue's midnight bounds the civil day (GC, SI, CL against MCXGOLD and MCXSILVER). Those were one value until 14-Sep-2026.

Source defects found in the 2026 document

Recorded rather than corrected, because a calendar that silently repairs its source cannot be audited against it.

  • B81 is labelled for the wrong planet. Its printed 2026 row is Venus's retrograde window to within four minutes, and the true Saturn∩Mercury window is the row B83 prints.
  • B82 reproduces only from the carry-in: Jupiter's retrograde began Nov-2025.
  • B114's printed end matches nothing in the sky; its second visit is printed nowhere.
  • B115's printed rows are the alone sub-windows, narrower than its title's union.
  • B88 is B87's series continuing with no verdict.
  • B30 defines its interval by longitude and never states what makes a planet Demoted or Shadow.

Blocked sections — 33, each naming what it waits for

A blocked section is a real condition the layer refuses to approximate. It is counted, emits nothing, and names the missing input.

  • B5 Mars in Pisces Navmansh (D9) — Mars's rashi windows while its navamsa is Pisces -- a residency rule over a D9 position, not a D9 ingress series, and the layer emits no Mars D9 ingress table because the source prints none
  • B6 Vargottam Mars — Vargottam Mars -- needs the D1 and D9 signs to agree at an instant, and the config already notes the source prints no Mars D9 ingress table to bound it
  • B10 Mercury Manifestation — a continuous Mercury-vs-Venus speed comparison. speed_deg_day is emitted only at event instants, so the date Mercury attains higher speed than Venus is not derivable from the astronomy layer
  • B11 Mercury - Furthest from Sun — a greatest-elongation event class. The astronomy layer emits elongation per record but never its extrema, and recovering a maximum from instants sampled at other events would be a scan, not a read
  • B19 Venus Ahead, Sun Behind and Mercury in the Middle — a benefic/malefic classification of the aspects on a body. The remark's verdict holds only 'provided there is a malefic aspect on Mercury'; the layer carries aspect records but no valence for them, and the source prints none either
  • B30 Demoted and Shadow Speed of Saturn — a rule, not merely the interval. B30 states when Saturn is in Demoted or Shadow Speed -- from 11-Dec-2026 until it crosses back over 20 deg 31' of Pisces direct on 15-Mar-2027 -- and its two printed values are VERIFIED to the arcminute (the engine puts Saturn at 20.508963 deg on 27-Jul-2026 and 20.507990 deg on 15-Mar-2027, and at 13.694991 deg on 11-Dec-2026). What the section never states is what makes a planet Demoted or Shadow: it names the band and the two dates and no condition. So the interval can be reproduced and the rule that generates it in another year cannot
  • B62 Chandra Darshan (New Moon) — a first-crescent visibility computation. The section's Tithi column reads Pratipada or Dwitiya, so the event is the sighting and not the conjunction; Step 3 measured swe.heliacal_ut against the source's own Venus rise dates and found it 9-10 days out, so the one routine available was rejected on evidence rather than on principle
  • B63 Hemisphere — a tropical solar longitude, or the equinox instant the layer would have to emit for one to be read. The equinox is a TROPICAL solar longitude of 0 or 180 degrees and every longitude the astronomy layer carries is sidereal ('lon_sid'), which is a frame the equinox slides through by about 50 arc seconds a year. The same record carries qa.ayanamsha_deg, so `lon_sid + ayanamsha_deg` reconstructs the tropical longitude at the instants the layer happens to sample the Sun -- but the Sun's own ingress series only marks whole signs, nakshatras and navamsas, which bracket an equinox date to 3 degrees 20 minutes, and the only dense solar series in the file is the per-venue horizon records, whose existence depends on a location rising. Pinning the date from those means interpolating a longitude between two of one venue's sunsets, and the rule layer is not licensed to reconstruct a longitude: measured, the interpolation reproduces the true equinox to about 5 minutes and the navamsa bracket to about 3.6 hours, so this is a licence question and not a numerical one <b>AND</b> a decision on what the range is and what breaks it. The note says 'Calculate range of the Hemisphere +/- 2/3 days any side' and never says the centre; and it says 'Breakout/breakdown is medium term trade' and 'When range is broken on both side, 2nd break is very powerful' without saying whether the range is a range of PRICES or the six-day window in TIME that the sentence before it just built. The word 'range' appears in both senses in the same line
  • B70 Big Volatile — Major Turning Days — the selection rule itself. The section states only that its dates "have been sorted on multiple parameters" and names none of them and no weighting; four candidate discriminators (lunation, station, sign ingress, inner-planet conjunction or slow-pair aspect) were tested and rejected, and all 51 dates carry at least one major configuration, so the list is over-determined and a fitted reconstruction would describe our fit rather than the source's rule
  • B71 Uttra Falguni Nakshtra During the Year — the Moon's navamsa ingress series. The Moon crosses a navamsa every two hours and the astronomy layer emits no navamsa ingress for it, which is the same absence that stops the navamsa ladder ranking the Moon in batch 2
  • B111 Moon Eclipse in Vaishak, Shravan or Ashwin Month — Bullish — the lunar month system. Naming a month Vaishakha, Shravana or Ashwin requires knowing whether the source counts months amanta or purnimanta -- the two disagree by a fortnight and therefore about which month an eclipse falls in. `month_system_confirmation` is open in config/conventions.yaml and this is a section it bounds
  • B116 Mercury in Paap Kartari — a benefic/malefic classification of the bodies. Paap Kartari is a hemming by malefics, and the section's own Planet-1/Planet-2 columns name the bodies that happen to hem Mercury in 2026 without ever stating what makes a body malefic. The same missing input blocks B19 and B117, and it is the third time it has been the binding constraint
  • B117 Jupiter in Paap Kartari — a benefic/malefic classification of the bodies. Paap Kartari is Jupiter hemmed between two malefics; the section's own Planet-1 and Planet-2 columns name the two for each printed row and never say what makes them malefic, and the astronomy layer carries each body's sign and nakshatra ingress but no valence for any of them. The identical absence blocks B19 in batch 2, whose verdict holds only 'provided there is a malefic aspect on Mercury'
  • B120 Mars Speed and Vedh — a threshold constrained by more than one crossing. Mars's speed crosses 0.658287 exactly ONCE in the whole of 2026, so the calibration solved one equation in one unknown: the feasible interval is just the speed's own change across the +/-1 day scoring window, and no other printed row in the year can falsify it. Zero degrees of freedom. The fit is therefore true by construction and carries no evidence, so the Vedha direction cannot be anchored to it. Mercury is the only inner planet whose level is overdetermined (six crossings); a later year supplying a second crossing for Mars would make this testable rather than re-derivable
  • B121 Jupiter Speed and Vedh — a slow-planet speed doctrine. Jupiter's Fast and Normal boundaries have no common speed level -- the two printed boundaries are 0.013750 (Jupiter) apart in threshold space. B30 'Demoted and Shadow Speed of Saturn' p.26 shows the slow planets answer to a different doctrine and defines its interval by LONGITUDE (Saturn at 20 deg 31' of Pisces, crossed retrograde 27-Jul-2026 and direct again 15-Mar-2027), supplying no speed level, so the class cannot be computed and the Vedha direction cannot be selected

Coverage — two denominators, and one of them is not 141

Instrument configuration sections — Chapter 2<section id="..."> with <h2>58 named groups38/58

Catalogue B is 141/141. The configuration sections are 38/58 ported, 20 blocked. The second set was never in the first's denominator — a different shape of markup, counted separately — so nothing on this page should be read as "the source is covered". The counts come from the document itself, not from this build's own config. The configuration rules live in their own registry and, as of this build, do not feed the rows below: porting a group is not publishing it, and the two are kept separate on purpose.

  • gold-bullish pp.136-144 — gold, bullish: 13 named groups, 7 ported, 6 blocked
  • gold-bearish pp.145-148 — gold, bearish: 6 named groups, 4 ported, 2 blocked
  • silver-bullish pp.149-161 — silver, bullish: 20 named groups, 15 ported, 5 blocked
  • silver-bearish pp.162-167 — silver, bearish: 10 named groups, 8 ported, 2 blocked
  • sugar-bullish pp.168-173 — sugar, bullish: 7 named groups, 3 ported, 4 blocked
  • sugar-bearish pp.174-175 — sugar, bearish: 2 named groups, 1 ported, 1 blocked

The 20 blocked groups, by the input each is missing: valence 9 · darshan 4 · month_system 3 · aspect_orb 2 · vedha_wheel 2 · no_dated_window 1. vedha_wheel is a sixth input the scope survey did not name and the port found; the other five are the survey's own.

Gold, silver and sugar are the three instruments the source prints verdicts for — that is what their tiers rest on — and their own configuration groups are unported: gold 19 · silver 30 · sugar 9. What they reach this calendar through today is generic catalogue-B rules whose bodies happen to resolve to them — a Venus rule reaches SUGAR because SUGAR's rulership is Venus, not because the source says anything about sugar. No row in this calendar originates in any configuration section: not one of the 5,209 rows carries a configuration section as its source, and that is still true after the port — the 38 ported groups are registered and fire against the 2027 sky, but nothing downstream reads them into this artifact yet.

There is a third unported body of material. The same chapter carries nine further <h2> sub-tables that are neither catalogue B nor any of the six blocks above (Kshin (Malefic) Moon, Total Days in Year, Rahu or Ketu Nakshtra on a Thursday, Moon Mercury in the Same Navamsh (D9), Rainfall Calculation, Mars With or Aspecting Mercury, Eclipse, Planet Vargottam in Their Own Nakshatra, Moon Rashi Parivartan Yog with Other Planets in D1), and the source's own monthly prophecy tables print named verdicts for gold and silver that are also outside catalogue B and also unported. Recorded because fixing one denominator and leaving the next one implicit only moves the misleading claim.

What porting the 58 groups would take is scoped per group in build/CONFIG_SECTIONS_SCOPE.md — not estimated. Of the 58, the survey classed 41 as needing no astronomy this layer lacks; the port delivered 38, because three of the 41 turned out to need an input the survey had not seen and one group it had not counted was ported as a resolved ambiguity. The estimate is kept beside the outcome rather than overwritten by it.

Why SUGAR's rows exist at all — a diagnosis that was wrong first

SUGAR'S ZERO WAS THE BODY-SCOPING FIX, AND THE FIX IS THE SECTOR ALIAS. Diagnosed rather than assumed, and the first diagnosis was WRONG: this note originally blamed only the unported blocks. The actual cause is that the rulership lookup asked for a `sugar` sector, and the table spells it `sugar_and_soft_goods` (from book_ch15's "sugar and soft/luxury goods"), so Venus resolved to nothing for that sector and the body-scoping step excluded SUGAR from every rule. Adding the alias restored it: SUGAR now emits 396 rows, 134 carrying a verdict and 262 null. The rows come from VENUS-ruled catalogue-B rules, which is the correct channel -- SUGAR's rulership is Venus per ch15, and this block's own `resolution` field says "SUGAR is tier 1 and takes its verdicts from the source's own configuration sections, so no rulership is needed to reach it". THE UNPORTED BLOCKS ABOVE ARE STILL A REAL GAP and still mean SUGAR's own nine named groups (pp.168-175) are not in the layer. They are the reason SUGAR's coverage is thin rather than the reason it was empty. Both facts are recorded; neither is allowed to hide the other.

Wording that admits more than one reading

  • B55 b055g_panchak_after_forty_ghati — '40 Ghati' is a time of day, and the sunrise series now fixes the instant it is counted from. What it does not fix is the length of the ghati, and the two readings in currency are not the same statement. Under the FIXED reading a ghati is 24 minutes -- a sixtieth of 24 hours, which is the sense B106 uses, correctly, because there it measures a DURATION and 24 minutes is a sixtieth of a day however the day is bounded. Under the VARIABLE reading a ghati is a sixtieth of the actual sunrise-to-sunrise day, which in Mumbai runs 23h58m to 24h02m across the year and in New York 23h46m to 24h14m. Forty ghati in is 16h00m under the first and up to nine minutes away from it under the second. The section prints no table of 40-ghati Panchaks -- its thirteen rows are the Panchak windows themselves, which both readings date identically -- so the document offers no row that could choose between them, and picking one would be this layer's decision rather than a reading of the page.
